newsitem.title: USA: USDA ready to unveil Conservation Reserve changes.
newsitem.headline: USDA ready to unveil Conservation Reserve changes.

text.p: Revisions to the Conservation Reserve Program, the major U.S. soil and water conservation program, will be unveiled Wednesday by Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman, it was announced.
A news conference was set for 1000 EDT/1400 GMT at USDA headquarters, Independence Avenue and 14th Street SW.
About 36.4 million acres were enrolled in the CRP, which pays farmers an annual rent to idle fragile land for 10 years.
Created in 1985 with an emphasis on prevention of soil erosion, CRP was given additional duties in the 1990 and 1996 farm laws to protect water purity and preserve wildlife habitat.
Under the new "Freedom to Farm" law, farmers were empowered to withdraw land from the CRP on 60 days' notice, a step intended to give them more flexibility to profit from high grain prices.

Response has been somewhat limited. Some analysts say farmers were deterred because they were unsure if they could return land to the CRP later. Congress has acted to put CRP rental rates in line with local rents.
